newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT says to benefit from peso's fall.
newsitem.headline: PLDT says to benefit from peso's fall.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co said on Tuesday it was expecting its net income to rise by 1.5 billion pesos over a year following the sharp depreciation of the peso.

"There will be some immediate translation gains because we have a slightly long dollar position. Our long distance rates are also effectively in dollars," PLDT executive vice-president and chief finance officer Edgardo del Fonso told Reuters.
Del Fonso said that the company stood to gain an additional 450 million pesos for every one peso depreciation.
He said PLDT can gain up to 1.5 billion pesos in additional net income if the peso stabilises at 29 pesos to a dollar for over a year.
PLDT sources about 50 percent of its revenues from international calls.
Del Fonso said that although a weakened peso would mean higher foreign debt service, the gains can easily offset the losses.

The Central Bank allowed the peso to float in a wider range last Friday after days of defending the peso from speculative attacks. On Tuesday, the peso ended unchanged at 29 pesos to a dollar. -- Manila newsroom (63 2) 8418939 Fax 8176267
